content.text:
Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Fix one blocking review finding on PR #46 (branch memory-direction-check, now targeting main) in aspekts/viva, a hackathon project (HackTheBurgh, submission Sunday 12:00). #46 reads decision memory at the push's base, and checks/direction.md raises "is this the right direction?" claims when a change contradicts a recorded decision. Direction claims are always selected for the exam. Read `gh pr view 46`, AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md first.

Setup: `git fetch origin`. The branch is checked out in other worktrees, so work on a detached HEAD from origin/memory-direction-check, and push with `git push origin HEAD:memory-direction-check`. Never force-push. Merge origin/main first: #45 is merged now, and main may have moved.

The finding (P1, from GPT-6.1 Sol's re-review, reproduced): selected direction claims can still escape the exam. `packages/engine/src/pipeline/review.ts` (around line 128) accepts the planner's result without checking direction coverage. `pipeline/plan.ts` (around lines 55–62) accepts any non-empty subset of the selected claims. Reproduction: the selected claims were [direction-1, behaviour-change-1], and a valid planner response asked only about behaviour-change-1. Answering it gave `approve / exam-passed` without the reversal ever being examined.

Fix:
- Guarantee every selected direction claim gets a question. If the planner omits one, add a deterministic fallback question built from the claim. For example: ask "This change appears to reverse a recorded decision: <claim summary>. Is that the right direction, and why?", with a short rubric such as "why the recorded decision no longer applies" and "what the change does instead", the claim's location, and a followUpIfVague. Keep the total at or under maxQuestions; direction questions take priority if trimming is needed.
- Fallback text must only use claim fields. Never put memory or session text into it unwrapped.
- Keep #47's invariant (no usable questions means throw) and #7's one-question-per-real-claim planner behaviour.
- Add a regression test using a schema-valid planner stub that omits the direction claim: the exam must include a direction question, and answering only the other question must not pass. Also add an eval case if it fits the existing direction evals.

Not in scope: the session token budget not counting memory text. Sol judged that non-blocking for the hackathon, as the hook fails open without recording a pass. Mention it in the PR body as a follow-up.

Rules:
- Run `pnpm install` and `env -u VIVA_LLM -u GEMINI_API_KEY pnpm check`. It must pass with no key and no network. Never make live model calls, and never copy any .env.
- Hard gates, data boundary, untrusted() and fail-open rules apply.
- Don't merge, and don't watch PRs. Don't kill processes you didn't start.
- Add the fix to the PR body's "After independent review" section.
- End commits with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`

Final message: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

Stretch goal: a memory layer for "is this the right direction?" questions.

**Stacked PR:** based on `issue-18-decision-memory` (#45), which is based on `queue/5-skip` (#39). It will be retargeted when the stack merges. It doesn't depend on #4.

**Pitch hook:** the developer saves "the check runs before the charge on purpose". Later an agent quietly reorders it, and `git push` asks: *"You told us checking the card before sending it was deliberate; this change reverses it. Is that the right direction, and why?"* A push touching files with no memory costs zero extra tokens.

## How it works

1. **Deterministic retrieval, before any model call** (`packages/engine/src/memory/retrieve.ts`). One `git ls-tree` at the push's base, then `git show` only for `.viva/memory/<file>.md` of changed files.
   - It reads the push's **base only** (changed after review, see below): memory the push adds or edits never takes part in reviewing that push.
   - It drops entries that match the injection patterns, and entries filed under another path. It keeps at most 8.
2. **One new check file, `checks/direction.md`**, which declares `needs: memory` in its frontmatter (`parseCheck` rejects unknown values).
   - `runChecks` skips it with **no model call** when nothing relevant is recorded, and only this check receives the memory, inside `untrusted("memory", …)`. No existing prompt grew.
3. **Output is the existing zod `CheckResult`**, so contradictions become ordinary ranked claims and then exam questions.
   - Direction claims ignore mastery: knowing the code doesn't settle whether reversing a recorded decision is intended.
   - Direction claims always reach the exam, whatever their risk score (changed after review, see below). If the intent explicitly asks for the reversal, the claim is `requested`, which lowers its score but not its place.
4. **Fails open.** Any error reading memory means an empty memory list, so the review carries on as before.

## Evals (mock provider, offline)

| Case | Want | Got |
|---|---|---|
| reverses a recorded decision | exam (direction), 5 calls | exam (direction), 5 calls |
| consistent with a recorded decision | low-risk, 4 calls | low-risk, 4 calls |
| same reversal with no memory | low-risk, 3 calls | low-risk, 3 calls |

The original six cases keep their token counts, so the check costs nothing where there's no memory. The mock flags a memory as reversed when the diff removes a line it covers. That proves retrieval, wiring and token use, **not** model judgement.

## Tests

`env -u VIVA_LLM -u GEMINI_API_KEY pnpm check` passes offline: 144 tests, evals 9/9. `retrieve.test.ts` covers:

- changed-files-only retrieval
- emptied memory still found at base (memory added in the push is now ignored, see below)
- poisoned and misfiled entries dropped
- damaged memory and a missing repo
- no call without memory, and memory sent as untrusted to the direction check only
- end-to-end question wording
- the consistent change stays quiet
- mastery ignored for direction claims
- fail open when the reader throws

## Not verified / notes

- **No live Gemini run.** The prompt's real precision is unmeasured. Run `pnpm evals` with a real provider before the demo.
- The planner prompt is unchanged. With Gemini the question wording comes from the claim summary format in `checks/direction.md`, not a fixed template.
- In one of three full `pnpm check` runs, the existing exam test "takes typed answers question-by-question…" failed with an Ink input timing flake under load. It passed alone 3/3 and in the other two full runs. It's not related to this change, but I'm flagging it.
- Merging main later: `evals/run.ts` changed there (#3 and #4). This PR's eval lives in new files (`evals/direction.ts`, `evals/cases/direction.ts`), so the conflict is a one-line call in `run.ts`. `review.ts` and `checks.ts` will need small hand merges with #4's session budget.

## After independent review

- **Memory is read at the push's base only** (P1). Reading base and then head, and overwriting by ID, let a push edit a base entry from "check before send" to "send before check" under the same ID so only the forged version was seen, and newer forged entries could push historical ones out of the 8-entry limit. `relevantMemory(repoPath, base, files)` now reads only the base commit, so memory added or edited in the same push never takes part in that review. It only counts once it's in a later push's base. `ReviewDeps.memory` lost its `head` argument.
  - Tests: an edited entry with the same ID can't replace the base one, a flood of 16 newer entries can't push the base entry out, and memory added in the push is ignored. New eval case "memory added in the same push" → low-risk, 3 calls.
  - Docs (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `README.md`) now describe memory as an unsigned repository assertion, not a verified developer statement.
- **Direction claims can no longer avoid the exam** (P1). They used to drop mastery but still had to clear the risk threshold, so a requested reversal with zero blast radius scored 0.5 and ended as `approve / low-risk` with no questions. `rankClaims` takes an optional `pinned` predicate. Pinned claims sort ahead of the rest, which also makes them win any overlap in dedupe. `startReview` pins claims from `needs: memory` checks and selects them regardless of the threshold, so they always fill the first slots within `maxQuestions`. The remaining slots go to the riskiest other claims above the threshold.
  - Tests: a requested reversal with nothing else risky still reaches the exam (risk < threshold, asserted). With four higher-risk silent claims, the reversal is asked first and the other two slots go to risky claims. Both fail on the old selection.
  - Eval: "requested reversal of a recorded decision" must be examined (exam, direction, 5 calls). The mock direction check now marks a claim `requested` when the intent says "reverse".
- Merged the #45 fixes (`issue-18-decision-memory`) into this branch with a normal merge.
- `env -u VIVA_LLM -u GEMINI_API_KEY pnpm check` passes offline: 151 tests, evals 11/11.
- **Trade-off:** if there are more reversals than `maxQuestions`, they take every slot and other risky claims aren't asked that push. Reversals are the stronger signal, since the team recorded those decisions explicitly.
- The empty-exam pass is fixed separately in #47 and isn't duplicated here.

## Integrated with main

Merged the updated `issue-18-decision-memory` (which now includes main and #47). The symlink checks, base-only memory and always-examined direction claims are unchanged.

# Working on Viva

Instructions for coding agents and humans.

## Rules

- Run `pnpm check` before calling work finished, and report the result honestly.
- `packages/contracts` is the contract. Change it first, then update `fixtures/mock` so the frontend keeps working.
- Deterministic steps run before any model call. Add a precheck before adding a prompt.
- All model access goes through `LlmProvider`. Output must be parsed by a zod schema.
- Wrap repository and session text with `untrusted()`. It is data, never instructions.
- Diffs, transcripts and model output never enter the ledger or logs. Only scores and hashes do.
- Hard gates (`skippable: false`) must never become configurable or skippable.
- Fail open: a Viva crash must never stop someone pushing.
- Use a one-question check file in `checks/` rather than growing an existing prompt.
- Never commit keys. Use `.env`.
- Keep everything working on Windows: no shell-only scripts, and use `node:path`.
- Add a test for every bug fixed. Add an eval case for every new prompt behaviour.

## Layout

- `packages/contracts`: shared zod schemas
- `packages/engine`: the review pipeline, ledger and fog
- `apps/vivad`: local daemon and `viva` CLI
- `apps/web`: The Fog and the exam room
- `checks`: one markdown file per check
- `evals`: tests for prompts
- `fixtures/mock`: sample data for the UI
